1	# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)
2	
3	Target: llama.cpp CPU backend on Andes RISC-V (AX45MPV-class, RVV 1.0, VLEN=512).
4	Baseline measured 2026-07-15 under Andes QEMU (VLEN=512, -t 8, noomp build):
5	Bonsai-4B Q1_0 ~19-21 s/token, 8B ~34-38 s/token, 27B ~124 s/token.
6	QEMU time tracks instruction count, not real latency - final numbers must come
7	from FPGA/hardware runs.
8	
9	Rules for every feature below:
10	- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
11	  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
12	  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
13	- Benchmark gate: llama-bench on QEMU (instruction-count proxy) + FPGA run
14	  (real latency) before/after. Keep per-feature commits separate.
15	
16	Status legend: TODO / IN-PROGRESS / DONE
17	
18	---
19	
20	## F0. CORRECTNESS: qwen35 (hybrid attention) produces garbage on rv64
21	
22	- Status: TODO - blocks all 27B work; fix before optimizing anything.
23	- Description: Bonsai-27B (arch qwen35, ~75% linear attention) generates
24	  incoherent text on rv64 QEMU while the same GGUF + prompt on x86 host
25	  answers correctly ("The capital of France is Paris."). Bonsai-4B/8B
26	  (plain qwen3) are coherent on rv64, and test-quantize-fns passes all 35
27	  quant types under QEMU (Q1_0/Q8_0 kernels exonerated). Suspect: the
28	  qwen35-only ops (delta-net / linear-attention recurrence, gating) in
29	  their RVV or fp16 (zvfh) paths, or a shape-dependent kernel edge case
30	  only the 27B tensor sizes hit.
31	- Evidence: scratchpad logs bonsai27b_long.log (garbage, 16 tokens, exit 0),
32	  host control run 2026-07-15 (correct, 10 t/s).
33	- Diagnosis plan:
34	  1. Rebuild rv64 with GGML_RVV=OFF (pure scalar); run 27B few tokens on
35	     QEMU. Scalar correct -> bug is in an RVV kernel; scalar also broken ->
36	     generic C op or fp16 ABI issue.
37	  2. Bisect op-level with llama-eval-callback: dump intermediate tensors
38	     host vs QEMU for one token, find first divergent op.
39	  3. Fix the kernel; add the failing case to test-backend-ops shapes.
40	- Key files:
41	  - src/models/ (qwen35 graph construction)
42	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp, vec.h (op implementations with __riscv_v/zvfh paths)
43	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/ (RVV kernels)
44	- Dependencies: none. Everything 27B-related depends on this.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)
49	
50	- Status: TODO
51	- Description: The Q1_0 dot kernel recomputes/reloads the same activations
52	  for every weight row. Set `.nrows = 2` (later 4) so one call computes 2
53	  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask
54	  load (vlm) + vmerge + reduce. Expected ~1.5-2x on the dominant matmul path.
55	- Key files:
56	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484-578 (vl256/vl128 kernels + dispatcher)
57	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:227-232 (.nrows field of GGML_TYPE_Q1_0)
58	- Dependencies: none. Best first step - small diff, big win.
59	
60	## F2. Q1_0 defer reductions + vector scale handling
61	
62	- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-16) - two candidate kernels implemented and
63	  verified in kernel-lab/ (q1_0.c): vl512 = per-group vl=32 + group sums
64	  packed into lanes via vslideup + vlse16 vector scales + one ordered
65	  reduction per row (zero vector->scalar moves in the block loop; correct
66	  for any VLEN >= 256); vl512w = same but vl=64 merges two groups (fewer
67	  instructions, extra slideup/slidedown data movement). All-VLEN correctness
68	  PASS. QEMU proxy on n=8192: vl256 57.5us, vl512w 64.9us, vl512 75.5us,
69	  generic 430us - see measurement note below: QEMU TCG makes vector
70	  instructions expensive and scalar ops ~free, so removing the 4 vmv.x.s +
71	  ~12 scalar float ops per block READS AS A REGRESSION under QEMU. The
72	  stall-removal benefit is only observable on vsim (rdcycle) or FPGA.
73	  Decision gate: vsim shootout vl256 vs vl512 vs vl512w before paste-back
74	  into ggml.
75	- Description: Today each 32-element group ends with vwredsum + scalar
76	  extract (vmv.x.s) + scalar fp16->fp32 + scalar FMA - the vector unit
77	  stalls 4x per block. Change to: (a) load activation scales for several
78	  blocks at once with strided load vlse16 (stride 34 = sizeof(block_q8_0)),
79	  widen once with vfwcvt; (b) collect group sums into vector lanes and do
80	  one vfmacc instead of 4 scalar FMAs; (c) unroll 2 blocks with two
81	  independent accumulator chains to hide latency. Expected ~1.3-1.5x.
82	- Key files:
83	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:500-518 (inner loop)
84	- Dependencies: independent of F1; combine after both proven.
85	
86	## F3. Q1_0 full-VLEN utilization
87	
88	- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-16) - finding from kernel-lab: because the
89	  Q8_0 activations are NOT contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a
90	  512-bit register costs slide instructions (vl512w: 2 vslideup + 2
91	  vslidedown per block) that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl
92	  alone cannot win for this vec_dot shape; the width pays off only via
93	  repack (F4, contiguous interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1,
94	  e.g. row A in lanes 0..31 / row B in lanes 32..63). Treat F3 as folded
95	  into F1/F4 rather than a standalone feature.
96	- Description: Kernel uses vl=32 at e8/LMUL=1, which fills only half a
97	  VLEN=512 register (VLMAX=64). Process 64 weights per step (vlm of 64
98	  mask bits) or a whole 128-weight block with e8m2. Scale application must
99	  still respect the per-32 Q8_0 groups (pair with F2's vector-scale path).
100	- Key files:
101	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484-521
102	- Dependencies: F2 (vector scale handling makes wider vl practical).
103	
104	## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)
105	
106	- Status: TODO - largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
107	- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
108	  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
109	  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
110	  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
111	    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
112	    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
113	    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
114	    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
115	  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
116	    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
117	    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
118	    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
119	    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
120	    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
121	- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
122	  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
123	  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
124	    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
125	  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
126	- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
127	  ```
128	  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
129	  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
130	      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
131	      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
132	      for c in 0..31:
133	          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
134	          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
135	          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
136	          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
137	      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
138	  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
139	  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs
140	  ```
141	  ~3 ops/col (1 vlm + vsub_vx + vadd_vx_m), all N-wide; ~393 N-wide ops per
142	  block-tile => ~6 ops/row/block at N=64 vs ~20 for single-row vec_dot, AND
143	  full VLMAX, AND no reduction stalls. Per-column vlm (128/block) is the
144	  main tuning point.
145	- N and LMUL mapping (answers "larger LMUL" for wide VLEN): fix N=64, adapt
146	  LMUL to vlenb at runtime so the fp32 accumulator is full: VLEN=2048->m1,
147	  1024->m2, 512->m4 (all give 64 fp32 lanes). One repacked type; nc must be
148	  a multiple of N=64 (typical hidden dims are; machinery handles remainder).

154	  * F4c - gemm (M>1 prefill): interleave activation rows too
155	    (ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0), reuse the accumulate with an M-tile. Dep: F4b.
156	  * F4d - wire into ggml: traits table + extra-buffer type + remove
157	    arch-fallback alias + pass test-quantize-fns / test-backend-ops. Dep: F4b.

159	  dot-product). F6 is Strategy B on the SAME repack layout - expand signs to
160	  +-1 int8 once, let NDS.VD4DOTS do the K-reduction in-lane. They compose;
161	  decision gate is a vsim A-vs-B shootout. Open question for user: is an
162	  int8 dot-product (zvqdotq / xandesvdot) available on the target? If yes,
163	  F6 may beat F4b; if no, F4b is the ceiling.

165	  - kernel-lab/ (F4a/F4b reference + test first, vsim shootout)
166	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp (repack fn + traits dispatch, ~line 3200 /
167	    3868 templates; 16x1 gemv reference at :1370)
168	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp (RVV microkernels; 8x8 at :114)
169	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.h (block<Q,N> types, gemv/gemm decls)

# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)

Target: llama.cpp CPU backend on Andes RISC-V (AX45MPV-class, RVV 1.0, VLEN=512).
Baseline measured 2026-07-15 under Andes QEMU (VLEN=512, -t 8, noomp build):
Bonsai-4B Q1_0 ~19-21 s/token, 8B ~34-38 s/token, 27B ~124 s/token.
QEMU time tracks instruction count, not real latency - final numbers must come
from FPGA/hardware runs.

Rules for every feature below:
- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
- Benchmark gate: llama-bench on QEMU (instruction-count proxy) + FPGA run
  (real latency) before/after. Keep per-feature commits separate.

Status legend: TODO / IN-PROGRESS / DONE

---

## F0. CORRECTNESS: qwen35 (hybrid attention) produces garbage on rv64

- Status: TODO - blocks all 27B work; fix before optimizing anything.
- Description: Bonsai-27B (arch qwen35, ~75% linear attention) generates
  incoherent text on rv64 QEMU while the same GGUF + prompt on x86 host
  answers correctly ("The capital of France is Paris."). Bonsai-4B/8B
  (plain qwen3) are coherent on rv64, and test-quantize-fns passes all 35
  quant types under QEMU (Q1_0/Q8_0 kernels exonerated). Suspect: the
  qwen35-only ops (delta-net / linear-attention recurrence, gating) in
  their RVV or fp16 (zvfh) paths, or a shape-dependent kernel edge case
  only the 27B tensor sizes hit.
- Evidence: scratchpad logs bonsai27b_long.log (garbage, 16 tokens, exit 0),
  host control run 2026-07-15 (correct, 10 t/s).
- Diagnosis plan:
  1. Rebuild rv64 with GGML_RVV=OFF (pure scalar); run 27B few tokens on
     QEMU. Scalar correct -> bug is in an RVV kernel; scalar also broken ->
     generic C op or fp16 ABI issue.
  2. Bisect op-level with llama-eval-callback: dump intermediate tensors
     host vs QEMU for one token, find first divergent op.
  3. Fix the kernel; add the failing case to test-backend-ops shapes.
- Key files:
  - src/models/ (qwen35 graph construction)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp, vec.h (op implementations with __riscv_v/zvfh paths)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/ (RVV kernels)
- Dependencies: none. Everything 27B-related depends on this.

---

## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)

- Status: TODO
- Description: The Q1_0 dot kernel recomputes/reloads the same activations
  for every weight row. Set `.nrows = 2` (later 4) so one call computes 2
  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask
  load (vlm) + vmerge + reduce. Expected ~1.5-2x on the dominant matmul path.
- Key files:

- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-16) - two candidate kernels implemented and

  reduction per row (zero vector->scalar moves in the block loop; correct

  instructions expensive and scalar ops ~free, so removing the 4 vmv.x.s +

  stall-removal benefit is only observable on vsim (rdcycle) or FPGA.

  stalls 4x per block. Change to: (a) load activation scales for several
  blocks at once with strided load vlse16 (stride 34 = sizeof(block_q8_0)),

  one vfmacc instead of 4 scalar FMAs; (c) unroll 2 blocks with two
  independent accumulator chains to hide latency. Expected ~1.3-1.5x.

  repack (F4, contiguous interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1,

  into F1/F4 rather than a standalone feature.

  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128

          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs

29	appends a node), then executes it in one shot via a generic per-node
30	dispatch loop (`ggml_graph_compute_thread` -> `ggml_compute_forward`, in
31	`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`). Individual ops are not distinguishable
32	at the call site (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code in
33	`src/models/qwen3.cpp` or similar) -- by the time any one op actually
34	*runs*, you are inside this generic loop, looking at a `ggml_tensor*`
35	with no easy way to tell "this is layer 7's V projection" apart from any
36	other `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` node without counting.
37	
38	So the marker patch counts nodes and fires on the K-th one:
39	
40	```c
41	// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, inside ggml_compute_forward's switch:
42	case GGML_OP_MUL_MAT:
43	    {
44	#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
45	        static int andesim_mul_mat_n = 0;
46	        const bool andesim_roi = (++andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K);
47	        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_begin();
48	#endif
49	        ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
50	#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
51	        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_end();
52	#endif
53	    } break;
54	```
55	
56	Also add near the top of the file:
57	
58	```c
59	#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
60	#include <andesim/ROI.h>
61	#endif
62	```
63	
64	`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` is a build-time `-D`, not a source edit -- picking
65	a different node to measure is a reconfigure, not a patch change (see
66	section 3). Both markers are HINT NOPs (`andesim_ROI_begin()`/`_end()`),
67	so this same binary still runs correctly, unmeasured, on any engine or on
68	silicon when the counter never reaches K (or when `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K`
69	is undefined -- the whole block compiles out).
70	
71	## 2. Counting the nodes
72	
73	Bonsai-4B (qwen3 architecture, 36 layers, 2560 embd) does 253 `MUL_MAT`
74	calls per token: 36 layers x 7 matmuls (Q, V, K, O-projection, FFN gate,
75	up, down -- confirmed via gdb breakpoint counting on a native x86 debug
76	build, not assumed from the layer count alone) + 1 final `lm_head`.
77	
78	## 3. Picking K: smallest matmul, not the first one that compiles
79	
80	The obvious first pick is any early node -- K=50 lands on layer 7's Q
81	projection (2560 -> 4096). It runs correctly (once the fixes in section 4
82	are applied) but is too large a computation for the cycle-accurate leg to
83	finish even inside a 900000ms (15 minute) `--step-timeout-ms` budget.
84	
85	Rather than guess a smaller K blindly, dump every node's operand shapes
86	for one real forward pass on a **native x86 build** (fast, no simulator
87	needed) with a throwaway diagnostic:
88	
89	```c
90	// temporary -- not committed; add right before ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(...):
91	#if defined(ANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES)
92	{
93	    const struct ggml_tensor* s0 = tensor->src[0];
94	    const struct ggml_tensor* s1 = tensor->src[1];
95	    fprintf(stderr, "ANDESIM_MUL_MAT name=%s src0=%s[%lldx%lld] src1=[%lldx%lld]\n",
96	            tensor->name, ggml_type_name(s0->type),
97	            (long long) s0->ne[0], (long long) s0->ne[1],
98	            (long long) s1->ne[0], (long long) s1->ne[1]);
99	}
100	#endif
101	```
102	
103	```sh
104	cmake -B build-host -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES"
105	cmake --build build-host -j --target llama-completion
106	./build-host/bin/llama-completion -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
107	  --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 1 -c 512 -t 1 2>&1 | grep ANDESIM_MUL_MAT
108	```
109	
110	Result, per layer: Q/O-projection and the FFN gate/up/down matmuls are
111	all 2560x4096..2560x9728 (the FFN matmuls are actually ~2.4x LARGER than
112	Q, not smaller -- do not assume "later in the layer means smaller"). The
113	K/V-projection (2560x1024, this model's grouped-query attention uses
114	fewer KV heads than Q heads) is the smallest matmul shape anywhere in the
115	architecture, ~4x fewer MACs than Q, ~9.6x fewer than the FFN matmuls,
116	and there is nothing smaller available in a standard transformer layer
117	(the `lm_head` is larger still: `2560 x vocab_size`).
118	
119	**Verified working value: `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51`** -- layer 7's V
120	projection, the very next node after the original K=50 pick. Completes
121	comfortably inside a 900000ms budget.
122	
123	If you retarget K, verify the object file actually recompiled with the
124	new value before spending 10+ minutes on a run that might still be
125	running the old K:
126	
127	```sh
128	python3 -c "
129	import json
130	for e in json.load(open('build-rv64-static/compile_commands.json')):
131	    if e['file'].endswith('ggml-cpu.c'):
132	        print(e['command']); break
133	" | grep -o 'ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=[0-9]*'
134	```
135	
136	(A stale-ccache-or-incomplete-incremental-rebuild gotcha cost real time
137	during this investigation: `compile_commands.json` showing the right flag
138	is necessary but was, once, not sufficient -- the `.o` had not actually
139	been regenerated. If a rebuild's *behavior* doesn't match what the
140	*compile command* implies, `rm -f` the exact `.o` path under
141	`build-rv64-static/ggml/src/CMakeFiles/ggml-cpu.dir/` and rebuild again
142	before doubting the fix itself.)
143	
144	## 4. Four fixes a real build needs before the cycle-accurate leg accepts it
145	
146	**These four fixes are specific to ELEN=32 engines** (`ax45mpv_premium`,
147	`ax46mpv_advanced`) and route around a vector-width limit those engines
148	genuinely have. On an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`) none of this is
149	needed -- the pristine upstream `ggml` source already works, because the
150	assumption these patches route around (e64 support) is actually true
151	there. Do not apply section 4's patches when building for an ELEN=64
152	engine; see section 8 for what THAT engine needs instead.
153	
154	Hybrid's QEMU leg is engine-synced (`elen=32`, from the accurate
155	`-readconfig`) -- unlike fast mode's own hardcoded, unconstrained `-cpu
156	andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` string, it actually enforces the real engine's
157	32-bit vector-element limit. A stock `GGML_RVV` build of `ggml` was
158	written assuming `v` implies the RVV-spec-mandated ELEN>=64 minimum, so
159	several code paths emit illegal 64-bit-element vector instructions this
160	target cannot execute. All four were found the same way: run the real
161	binary, catch the illegal-instruction trap (mcause=2), disassemble at the
162	exact `mepc`, fix, repeat.
163	
164	1. **`ggml_vec_dot_f16`/`ggml_vec_dot_bf16`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp`):
165	   GCC auto-vectorizes their `double`-accumulated scalar fallback loop
166	   (taken because this build has neither `__riscv_zvfh` nor
167	   `__riscv_zvfbfwma`) into an illegal widening e64 reduce. Fix: add
168	   `__attribute__((target("arch=rv64gc")))` to just these two function
169	   definitions -- confirmed empirically that GCC's RISC-V port honors a
170	   function-level `target` attribute for suppressing this (the `optimize`
171	   attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`/`optimize` do NOT work here --
172	   tried both, objdump showed no change either time).
173	
174	2. **`ggml_vec_cvar_f32`/`ggml_vec_soft_max_f32`** (same file): use an
175	   explicit `vfloat64m1_t` accumulator (`vfwredusum_vs_f32m2_f64m1`,
176	   widening reduce). Every other architecture's branch in these same two
177	   functions reduces in native f32 precision with a plain SIMD op, then
178	   widens ONE scalar partial-sum per chunk to `double` in ordinary C --
179	   the RISC-V branch was the only outlier, not a hardware requirement.
180	   Fix: rewrite to match the sibling pattern (`vfredusum_vs_f32m2_f32m1`,
181	   non-widening, then `sum += (ggml_float) partial` in scalar C). Zero e64,
182	   same numerics every other build already computes.
183	
184	3. **`quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1`**
185	   (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`): hardcode `vfloat32m8_t`
186	   (LMUL=8) for `vfabs`/`vfredmax`, unconditionally, unlike every other
187	   quant kernel in the same file (which dispatch across
188	   vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128 variants). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU
189	   datapath does not extend to LMUL=8 for floating-point ops specifically
190	   (a plain integer `vle32.v` load at the same LMUL=8 executes fine
191	   immediately before the float op faults -- this is FP-datapath-specific,
192	   not a blanket LMUL cap; correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config
193	   bit, though only vsim's RTL enforces it -- QEMU does not, which is why
194	   this one surfaces on vsim rather than QEMU1, unlike fixes 1/2/4). Fix:
195	   both functions now call their existing portable `_ref` scalar
196	   implementations (`ggml/src/ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV
197	   fallback everywhere) unconditionally -- this is activation
198	   quantization, called once per token row before the (still fully
199	   vectorized) dot-product loop reuses it, a trivial fraction of total
200	   matmul cost.
201	
202	4. **Diagnostic-path gap, not a ggml bug**: `runtime/handler.c`'s trap
203	   handler (shared by every andesim runtime, vplat and vlinux alike)
204	   calls `fprintf` then `_exit()`; `_exit()` never flushes stdio, so on a
205	   fully-buffered stderr (the vlinux syscall-backed stdio path) the whole
206	   diagnostic was silently lost on every trap. Fixed with an
207	   `fflush(stderr)` before `_exit()`, plus a raw `htif_uart_putc()`-based
208	   emergency print of `mcause`/`mepc`/`mtval` before even attempting
209	   `fprintf` (cheap insurance against a corrupted-state trap taking out
210	   `fprintf` itself). This is what made fix 3 possible to diagnose in the
211	   first place -- see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s U9 section for the full
212	   trail.
213	
214	## 5. Reproducing the confirmed run
215	
216	```sh
217	# in llama.cpp:
218	cmake -B build-rv64-static \
219	  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
220	  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
221	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
222	  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
223	cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
224	
225	# in andesim:
226	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
227	  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
228	  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
229	  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
230	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
231	```
232	
233	Expected: `[andesim] 6528953 cycles`, identical across repeat runs.
234	
235	## 6. Measuring N consecutive iterations
236	
237	For a few consecutive matmuls instead of just one, set `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N`
238	alongside `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` (both are build-time `-D`s -- no source
239	change). The marker begins at node K and ends at node K+N-1, so N=1
240	(the default when unset) is exactly the original single-iteration
241	behavior:
242	
243	```sh
244	cmake -B build-rv64-static ... \
245	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..." \
246	  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..."
247	cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
248	```
249	
250	Confirmed K=51..52 (V then K projection, both small): **13040043
251	cycles**, ~2x the single-iteration figure as expected.
252	
253	**Keep N small.** The cycle-accurate leg runs at ~9 kHz; N=1 on the V
254	projection alone already needs ~13 minutes of wall clock (hence
255	`--step-timeout-ms 900000`+). Including one of the large matmuls (Q, O,
256	or any FFN projection -- see section 3's size ranking) in the range
257	multiplies the cost accordingly; a whole token (253 matmuls) is not
258	practical this way. Pick a short, deliberately small run of the
259	smallest-available matmuls, exactly like section 3 already argues for
260	a single iteration.
261	
262	## 7. Dumping pipeline information (`--kanata`)
263	
264	`andesim run --mode hybrid --kanata <file>` (see USER_GUIDE.md section
265	5.8) writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace of the ROI, viewable in
266	[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata):
267	
268	```sh
269	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
270	  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
271	  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata \
272	  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
273	  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
274	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
275	```
276	
277	No source or build change needed beyond what section 5 already has --
278	`--kanata` reads the same ROI markers the cycle measurement uses.
279	Confirmed on the K=51 single-iteration build: a 651 MB, well-formed
280	Kanata trace (`Kanata 0004` header, ~43.8M lines, event counts
281	consistent with 6528953 cycles). The trace is large in proportion to
282	the cycle count -- expect a correspondingly bigger file for a
283	multi-iteration (N>1) ROI.
284	
285	**A real bug this surfaced, fixed as part of this work**: the driver's
286	`vsim_extra_args()` (`driver/hybrid.cpp`) unconditionally appended a
287	`--kanata-roi` flag alongside `--kanata` -- a flag that does not exist
288	anywhere in vsim (confirmed against vsim's own `--help` and its full
289	source tree), so every hybrid `--kanata` run failed immediately with
290	`Unrecognized option: --kanata-roi` before this fix. Root cause: vsim's
291	hybrid leg only ever executes the ROI in the first place (it resumes
292	at the trigger boundary and exits on the matching trigger), so plain
293	`--kanata` already produces exactly the "measured window only" trace
294	USER_GUIDE.md section 5.8 describes -- no separate "roi" flag was ever
295	needed on vsim's side. This had no automated-test coverage (the only
296	place `--kanata-roi` appeared besides the driver's own code was a
297	manually-gated block in `tests/e2e.sh` behind an unset-by-default
298	`KANATA_FILE` env var), so the bug was latent until `--kanata` was
299	actually exercised against a real vsim binary for the first time here.
300	
301	## 8. Building for an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`)
302	
303	This engine's real ISA has Zca+Zcmp+Zcmt but NOT Zcd (compressed
304	double-precision FP load/store) -- confirmed via
305	`sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --print-qemu-config`, the ground-truth source for
306	any engine's real capability set (never assume it from a same-family
307	engine's config; `ax46mpv_advanced`, sharing the same `cpp_wrapper`, is
308	single-bank-HVM and Zcd-agnostic in a way `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` is not).
309	GCC's default `rv64gc...` march sets the legacy monolithic `C` bit,
310	which implies Zcd -- so ordinary function prologues spilling
311	callee-saved FP registers (nothing ROI/vector-specific; this hit
312	`ggml_cpu_init`, generic ggml startup code) emitted `c.fsdsp`, illegal
313	on this chip. Two new CMake cache variables in
314	`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt` let the march string target this
315	correctly, with the default (`GGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS` unset ==
316	`"gc"`, `GGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA` unset == none) reproducing the EXACT prior
317	march string for every other engine, unchanged:
318	
319	```sh
320	# in llama.cpp (no vec.cpp/quants.c/march-restriction patches applied --
321	# pristine upstream source, section 4 is NOT needed on this engine):
322	cmake -B build-rv64-static \
323	  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
324	  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
325	  -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
326	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
327	  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
328	cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
329	
330	# in andesim: this engine's cycle-accurate leg is MUCH slower in
331	# wall-clock terms than ax45mpv_premium's for the same node (several
332	# hundred x realtime vs ax45's tens of x) -- budget --step-timeout-ms
333	# generously; 900000 (the ax45mpv_premium-sized default) is NOT enough
334	# even for a single K=51 iteration on this engine.
335	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
336	  --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
337	  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
338	  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
339	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
340	```
341	
342	Expected: `[andesim] 4476168 cycles`.
343	
344	**A second, unrelated bug found getting here, fixed in the external
345	`vsim_andesim` repo, not andesim or llama.cpp**: this is the first
346	ax46mpv-family engine config with `NDS_HVM_BANKS=2` (every prior
347	ax46mpv config, e.g. `ax46mpv_advanced`, is single-bank).
348	`ax46mpv_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s `set_hvm`/`get_hvm` only ever
349	wrote/read HVM bank0's hierarchical Verilated array, using the TOTAL
350	`_NDS_HVM_SIZE_KB` (both banks combined) as the length -- overflowing
351	bank0's actual (half-sized) array by the other half, corrupting heap
352	state that only surfaced later as an unrelated-looking SIGSEGV inside
353	`sc_core::sc_port_registry::construction_done()` during the NEXT
354	`sc_start()` elaboration call. Fixed by porting
355	`ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s already-correct 2-bank
356	split (same shared `hvm_bank_write`/`hvm_bank_read` helpers,
357	`lm_backdoor.hpp`, called twice with different `base` offsets) into
358	ax46mpv's wrapper, gated so the existing single-bank engine's behavior
359	is untouched. Rebuilt via `vsim_andesim/build_vsim.sh` (the repo's own
360	Docker/podman build, no manual host-side ninja invocation -- the
361	generated build files reference container-internal `/work/...` paths).
362	If a future engine changes any other previously-constant parameter
363	(cache presence/level, privilege levels, bank counts elsewhere), expect
364	a similar class of latent bug in whichever cpu_wrapper code path was
365	never exercised with that parameter varying.

# Measuring one llama.cpp kernel iteration under andesim hybrid mode

This is the companion doc USER_GUIDE.md section 11 points to: the exact
patch that puts ROI markers around a matmul (or a short run of
consecutive matmuls) inside llama.cpp, how the target was chosen, and
the upstream `ggml` fixes a real build needs before it survives the
cycle-accurate leg's ELEN=32 vector unit.

Confirmed end to end:
- 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51, layer 7's V projection), on
  `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (ELEN=32) -- **6528953 cycles**, stable across
  two independent hybrid runs.
- 2026-07-16: two consecutive iterations (K=51..52, V then K
  projection), same engine -- **13040043 cycles** (~2x the
  single-iteration figure, as expected for two similarly-sized matmuls
  back to back). See section 6 for how to pick N.
- 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51), on `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3`
  (ELEN=64, VLEN=1024, first engine with a real L3 cache) -- **4476168
  cycles**, with the PRISTINE upstream `ggml` source (none of section
  4's three ggml patches applied -- this engine's real ELEN=64 vector
  unit runs the original e64 code natively). Fewer cycles than
  ax45mpv_premium's for the SAME node: the doubled VLEN does more work
  per vector instruction. See section 8 for this engine's build recipe
  and two DIFFERENT bugs that needed fixing to get there.

## 1. Why the marker goes in ggml's dispatch loop, not llama.cpp's model code

`ggml` builds its WHOLE computation graph first (`ggml_mul_mat()` just
appends a node), then executes it in one shot via a generic per-node
dispatch loop (`ggml_graph_compute_thread` -> `ggml_compute_forward`, in
`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`). Individual ops are not distinguishable
at the call site (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code in
`src/models/qwen3.cpp` or similar) -- by the time any one op actually
*runs*, you are inside this generic loop, looking at a `ggml_tensor*`
with no easy way to tell "this is layer 7's V projection" apart from any
other `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` node without counting.

So the marker patch counts nodes and fires on the K-th one:

```c
// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, inside ggml_compute_forward's switch:
case GGML_OP_MUL_MAT:
    {
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        static int andesim_mul_mat_n = 0;
        const bool andesim_roi = (++andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K);
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_begin();
#endif
        ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_end();
#endif
    } break;
```

Also add near the top of the file:

```c
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
#include <andesim/ROI.h>
#endif
```

`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` is a build-time `-D`, not a source edit -- picking
a different node to measure is a reconfigure, not a patch change (see
section 3). Both markers are HINT NOPs (`andesim_ROI_begin()`/`_end()`),
so this same binary still runs correctly, unmeasured, on any engine or on
silicon when the counter never reaches K (or when `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K`
is undefined -- the whole block compiles out).

## 2. Counting the nodes

Bonsai-4B (qwen3 architecture, 36 layers, 2560 embd) does 253 `MUL_MAT`
calls per token: 36 layers x 7 matmuls (Q, V, K, O-projection, FFN gate,
up, down -- confirmed via gdb breakpoint counting on a native x86 debug
build, not assumed from the layer count alone) + 1 final `lm_head`.

## 3. Picking K: smallest matmul, not the first one that compiles

The obvious first pick is any early node -- K=50 lands on layer 7's Q
projection (2560 -> 4096). It runs correctly (once the fixes in section 4
are applied) but is too large a computation for the cycle-accurate leg to
finish even inside a 900000ms (15 minute) `--step-timeout-ms` budget.

Rather than guess a smaller K blindly, dump every node's operand shapes
for one real forward pass on a **native x86 build** (fast, no simulator
needed) with a throwaway diagnostic:

```c
// temporary -- not committed; add right before ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(...):
#if defined(ANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES)
{
```

## 4. Four fixes a real build needs before the cycle-accurate leg accepts it

**These four fixes are specific to ELEN=32 engines** (`ax45mpv_premium`,
`ax46mpv_advanced`) and route around a vector-width limit those engines
genuinely have. On an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`) none of this is
needed -- the pristine upstream `ggml` source already works, because the
assumption these patches route around (e64 support) is actually true
there. Do not apply section 4's patches when building for an ELEN=64
engine; see section 8 for what THAT engine needs instead.

Hybrid's QEMU leg is engine-synced (`elen=32`, from the accurate
`-readconfig`) -- unlike fast mode's own hardcoded, unconstrained `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` string, it actually enforces the real engine's
32-bit vector-element limit. A stock `GGML_RVV` build of `ggml` was
written assuming `v` implies the RVV-spec-mandated ELEN>=64 minimum, so
several code paths emit illegal 64-bit-element vector instructions this
target cannot execute. All four were found the same way: run the real
binary, catch the illegal-instruction trap (mcause=2), disassemble at the
exact `mepc`, fix, repeat.

1. **`ggml_vec_dot_f16`/`ggml_vec_dot_bf16`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp`):
   GCC auto-vectorizes their `double`-accumulated scalar fallback loop
   (taken because this build has neither `__riscv_zvfh` nor
   `__riscv_zvfbfwma`) into an illegal widening e64 reduce. Fix: add
   `__attribute__((target("arch=rv64gc")))` to just these two function
   definitions -- confirmed empirically that GCC's RISC-V port honors a
   function-level `target` attribute for suppressing this (the `optimize`
   attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`/`optimize` do NOT work here --
   tried both, objdump showed no change either time).

2. **`ggml_vec_cvar_f32`/`ggml_vec_soft_max_f32`** (same file): use an
   explicit `vfloat64m1_t` accumulator (`vfwredusum_vs_f32m2_f64m1`,
   widening reduce). Every other architecture's branch in these same two
   functions reduces in native f32 precision with a plain SIMD op, then
   widens ONE scalar partial-sum per chunk to `double` in ordinary C --
   the RISC-V branch was the only outlier, not a hardware requirement.
   Fix: rewrite to match the sibling pattern (`vfredusum_vs_f32m2_f32m1`,
   non-widening, then `sum += (ggml_float) partial` in scalar C). Zero e64,
   same numerics every other build already computes.

3. **`quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1`**
   (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`): hardcode `vfloat32m8_t`
   (LMUL=8) for `vfabs`/`vfredmax`, unconditionally, unlike every other
   quant kernel in the same file (which dispatch across
   vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128 variants). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU
   datapath does not extend to LMUL=8 for floating-point ops specifically
   (a plain integer `vle32.v` load at the same LMUL=8 executes fine
   immediately before the float op faults -- this is FP-datapath-specific,
   not a blanket LMUL cap; correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config
   bit, though only vsim's RTL enforces it -- QEMU does not, which is why
   this one surfaces on vsim rather than QEMU1, unlike fixes 1/2/4). Fix:
   both functions now call their existing portable `_ref` scalar
   implementations (`ggml/src/ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV
   fallback everywhere) unconditionally -- this is activation
   quantization, called once per token row before the (still fully
   vectorized) dot-product loop reuses it, a trivial fraction of total
   matmul cost.

4. **Diagnostic-path gap, not a ggml bug**: `runtime/handler.c`'s trap
   handler (shared by every andesim runtime, vplat and vlinux alike)
   calls `fprintf` then `_exit()`; `_exit()` never flushes stdio, so on a
   fully-buffered stderr (the vlinux syscall-backed stdio path) the whole
   diagnostic was silently lost on every trap. Fixed with an
   `fflush(stderr)` before `_exit()`, plus a raw `htif_uart_putc()`-based
   emergency print of `mcause`/`mepc`/`mtval` before even attempting
   `fprintf` (cheap insurance against a corrupted-state trap taking out
   `fprintf` itself). This is what made fix 3 possible to diagnose in the
   first place -- see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s U9 section for the full
   trail.

## 5. Reproducing the confirmed run

```sh
# in llama.cpp:
cmake -B build-rv64-static \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion

# in andesim:
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

Expected: `[andesim] 6528953 cycles`, identical across repeat runs.

## 6. Measuring N consecutive iterations

For a few consecutive matmuls instead of just one, set `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N`
alongside `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` (both are build-time `-D`s -- no source
change). The marker begins at node K and ends at node K+N-1, so N=1
(the default when unset) is exactly the original single-iteration
behavior:

```sh
cmake -B build-rv64-static ... \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..." \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..."
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
```

Confirmed K=51..52 (V then K projection, both small): **13040043
cycles**, ~2x the single-iteration figure as expected.

**Keep N small.** The cycle-accurate leg runs at ~9 kHz; N=1 on the V
projection alone already needs ~13 minutes of wall clock (hence
`--step-timeout-ms 900000`+). Including one of the large matmuls (Q, O,
or any FFN projection -- see section 3's size ranking) in the range
multiplies the cost accordingly; a whole token (253 matmuls) is not
practical this way. Pick a short, deliberately small run of the
smallest-available matmuls, exactly like section 3 already argues for
a single iteration.

## 7. Dumping pipeline information (`--kanata`)

`andesim run --mode hybrid --kanata <file>` (see USER_GUIDE.md section
5.8) writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace of the ROI, viewable in
[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata):

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata \
  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

No source or build change needed beyond what section 5 already has --
`--kanata` reads the same ROI markers the cycle measurement uses.
Confirmed on the K=51 single-iteration build: a 651 MB, well-formed
Kanata trace (`Kanata 0004` header, ~43.8M lines, event counts
consistent with 6528953 cycles). The trace is large in proportion to
the cycle count -- expect a correspondingly bigger file for a
multi-iteration (N>1) ROI.

**A real bug this surfaced, fixed as part of this work**: the driver's
`vsim_extra_args()` (`driver/hybrid.cpp`) unconditionally appended a
`--kanata-roi` flag alongside `--kanata` -- a flag that does not exist
anywhere in vsim (confirmed against vsim's own `--help` and its full
source tree), so every hybrid `--kanata` run failed immediately with
`Unrecognized option: --kanata-roi` before this fix. Root cause: vsim's
hybrid leg only ever executes the ROI in the first place (it resumes
at the trigger boundary and exits on the matching trigger), so plain
`--kanata` already produces exactly the "measured window only" trace
USER_GUIDE.md section 5.8 describes -- no separate "roi" flag was ever
needed on vsim's side. This had no automated-test coverage (the only
place `--kanata-roi` appeared besides the driver's own code was a
manually-gated block in `tests/e2e.sh` behind an unset-by-default
`KANATA_FILE` env var), so the bug was latent until `--kanata` was
actually exercised against a real vsim binary for the first time here.

## 8. Building for an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`)

This engine's real ISA has Zca+Zcmp+Zcmt but NOT Zcd (compressed
double-precision FP load/store) -- confirmed via
`sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --print-qemu-config`, the ground-truth source for
any engine's real capability set (never assume it from a same-family
engine's config; `ax46mpv_advanced`, sharing the same `cpp_wrapper`, is
single-bank-HVM and Zcd-agnostic in a way `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` is not).
GCC's default `rv64gc...` march sets the legacy monolithic `C` bit,
which implies Zcd -- so ordinary function prologues spilling
callee-saved FP registers (nothing ROI/vector-specific; this hit
`ggml_cpu_init`, generic ggml startup code) emitted `c.fsdsp`, illegal
on this chip. Two new CMake cache variables in
`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt` let the march string target this
correctly, with the default (`GGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS` unset ==
`"gc"`, `GGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA` unset == none) reproducing the EXACT prior
march string for every other engine, unchanged:

```sh
# in llama.cpp (no vec.cpp/quants.c/march-restriction patches applied --
# pristine upstream source, section 4 is NOT needed on this engine):
cmake -B build-rv64-static \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
  -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion

# in andesim: this engine's cycle-accurate leg is MUCH slower in
# wall-clock terms than ax45mpv_premium's for the same node (several
# hundred x realtime vs ax45's tens of x) -- budget --step-timeout-ms
# generously; 900000 (the ax45mpv_premium-sized default) is NOT enough
# even for a single K=51 iteration on this engine.
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

Expected: `[andesim] 4476168 cycles`.

**A second, unrelated bug found getting here, fixed in the external
`vsim_andesim` repo, not andesim or llama.cpp**: this is the first
ax46mpv-family engine config with `NDS_HVM_BANKS=2` (every prior
ax46mpv config, e.g. `ax46mpv_advanced`, is single-bank).
`ax46mpv_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s `set_hvm`/`get_hvm` only ever
wrote/read HVM bank0's hierarchical Verilated array, using the TOTAL
`_NDS_HVM_SIZE_KB` (both banks combined) as the length -- overflowing
bank0's actual (half-sized) array by the other half, corrupting heap
state that only surfaced later as an unrelated-looking SIGSEGV inside
`sc_core::sc_port_registry::construction_done()` during the NEXT
`sc_start()` elaboration call. Fixed by porting
`ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s already-correct 2-bank
split (same shared `hvm_bank_write`/`hvm_bank_read` helpers,
`lm_backdoor.hpp`, called twice with different `base` offsets) into
ax46mpv's wrapper, gated so the existing single-bank engine's behavior
is untouched. Rebuilt via `vsim_andesim/build_vsim.sh` (the repo's own
Docker/podman build, no manual host-side ninja invocation -- the
generated build files reference container-internal `/work/...` paths).
If a future engine changes any other previously-constant parameter
(cache presence/level, privilege levels, bank counts elsewhere), expect
a similar class of latent bug in whichever cpu_wrapper code path was
never exercised with that parameter varying.

# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai-4B Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)

Primary model: models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (572 MB, arch qwen3, 36 layers,
embd 2560, GQA with 1024-wide K/V projections, 253 MUL_MAT nodes per token
= 36 x 7 + lm_head).

Why 4B (decision 2026-07-21, replaces the old 27B focus):
- Fits andesim hybrid's hard 2 GiB guest-RAM cap with room for KV cache and
  compute buffers (27B needs ~4.5 GB - blocked until andesim grows >2 GiB
  DRAM support).
- Plain qwen3: output is coherent on rv64. The qwen35 hybrid-attention bug
  (old F0) only affects 27B, so it no longer blocks anything - parked below.
- The full closed loop already works on 4B: end-to-end cycle-accurate
  per-kernel measurement under andesim hybrid marker mode was confirmed
  2026-07-16 (see Measurement setup).

Hardware targets (both vsim engines, VLEN 512-2048 family per F4 design):
- vsim:ax45mpv_premium - VLEN=512, DLEN=512, ELEN=32, no zfh/zvfh.
- vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 - VLEN=1024, ELEN=64, first engine with real L3.

Baselines:
- QEMU proxy (insn-count, -t 8, build-rv64-noomp, 2026-07-15):
  4B ~19-21 s/token. QEMU time tracks instruction count, not latency.
- Real cycles, hybrid marker ROI at K=51 (layer 7 V projection, 2560x1024,
  the smallest matmul in the model - nothing smaller exists per-layer):
  - ax45mpv_premium: 6528953 cycles (2026-07-16, stable across runs)
  - ax46mpv_fpga_l3: 4476168 cycles (2026-07-16, pristine upstream ggml)
  These are THE per-kernel before/after gate for F1-F7: same K, same model,
  real pipeline + memory system.

Rules for every feature below:
- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
- Benchmark gate: QEMU proxy for correctness + rough insn counts, then
  hybrid marker ROI cycles before/after (the real number). FPGA only for
  final full-token figures.

ELEN=32 constraint (ax45mpv_premium): no 64-bit vector elements anywhere.
Stock repack.cpp uses __riscv_vsseg4e64 -> GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF today; any
new F4 kernel must stay e32-clean (the Nx1 design already is: vlm masks,
int16 sumi, fp32 accumulators). Also: premium's FP datapath rejects LMUL=8
float ops (integer LMUL=8 is fine) - F4's VLEN=512 -> m4 fp32 mapping is
exactly at the safe limit; never use m8 for float.

- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-16) - two candidate kernels implemented and

  reduction per row (zero vector->scalar moves in the block loop; correct
  for any VLEN >= 256); vl512w = same but vl=64 merges two groups (fewer
  instructions, extra slideup/slidedown data movement). All-VLEN correctness

  ops ~free, so removing the 4 vmv.x.s + ~12 scalar float ops per block

  vl256 vs vl512 vs vl512w - now doable in-model via the K=51 marker ROI

  extract (vmv.x.s) + scalar fp16->fp32 + scalar FMA - the vector unit
  stalls 4x per block. Change to: (a) load activation scales for several
  blocks at once with strided load vlse16 (stride 34 = sizeof(block_q8_0)),
  widen once with vfwcvt; (b) collect group sums into vector lanes and do
  one vfmacc instead of 4 scalar FMAs; (c) unroll 2 blocks with two
  independent accumulator chains to hide latency. Expected ~1.3-1.5x.

- Dependencies: independent of F1; combine after both proven.

- Status: folded (2026-07-16 finding) - because Q8_0 activations are NOT
  contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a 512-bit register costs slide
  instructions that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl alone cannot
  win for the vec_dot shape; width pays off only via repack (F4, contiguous
  interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1). Not a standalone feature.

## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)

- Status: TODO - largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
  ```
  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
      for c in 0..31:
          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs
  ```
  ~3 ops/col (1 vlm + vsub_vx + vadd_vx_m), all N-wide; ~393 N-wide ops per
  block-tile => ~6 ops/row/block at N=64 vs ~20 for single-row vec_dot, AND
  full VLMAX, AND no reduction stalls. Per-column vlm (128/block) is the
  main tuning point. Everything is e8/e16/e32 - ELEN=32-clean by design.
- N and LMUL mapping: fix N=64, adapt LMUL to vlenb at runtime so the fp32
  accumulator is full: VLEN=2048->m1, 1024->m2 (fpga_l3), 512->m4 (premium,
  FP-LMUL limit respected). One repacked type; nc must be a multiple of
  N=64 (2560 and 1024 both are; machinery handles remainder).

  * F4b - RVV row-parallel gemv (loop above), N=64 LMUL-adaptive. Dep: F4a.

## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)

- Status: TODO - largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
  ```
  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
      for c in 0..31:
          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs
  ```
  ~3 ops/col (1 vlm + vsub_vx + vadd_vx_m), all N-wide; ~393 N-wide ops per
  block-tile => ~6 ops/row/block at N=64 vs ~20 for single-row vec_dot, AND
  full VLMAX, AND no reduction stalls. Per-column vlm (128/block) is the
  main tuning point. Everything is e8/e16/e32 - ELEN=32-clean by design.
- N and LMUL mapping: fix N=64, adapt LMUL to vlenb at runtime so the fp32
  accumulator is full: VLEN=2048->m1, 1024->m2 (fpga_l3), 512->m4 (premium,
  FP-LMUL limit respected). One repacked type; nc must be a multiple of
  N=64 (2560 and 1024 both are; machinery handles remainder).

/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */
